subject: Sales discovery: model routing & integration follow-up
messages:
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 02 Mar 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery call recap — integration & routing topics

Hi Alice — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we all have the same page: 

Key notes from discovery:
- Primary workload: customer support search + generation for knowledge base (200-500 QPS expected at peak).
- Latency target: p95 <= 200ms for single-turn queries; cost sensitivity for back-office batch queries.
- Data residency: US + EU regions; sensitive PII stored in customer DB (we will need KMS + audit logs).
- Integration: front-end will call our SDK via backend service; embeddings index lives in your vector DB.

Recommended integration & architecture follow-ups (actionable):
1) SDK & auth
   - We recommend starting with the Redwood SDK quickstart (attached) for node/python.
   - Auth options: API keys for dev/proof-of-concept; OAuth or service-account keys + KMS for production/Private deployment.
   - If you require SSO + SCIM for user provisioning, we can map that in the next call.

2) Model routing & policy (high-level)
   - Primary model: redwood-rt-lowlat (quantized) in us-east for user-facing queries.
   - Fallback chain: redwood-rt-lowlat -> redwood-llama-13b-quant -> redwood-llama-7b-quant (degrades cost first, then latency).
   - Policy types supported: latency-first, cost-first (soft thresholds), region-routing (route EU requests to eu-west replica), and custom tenant overrides.
   - Suggested p95 SLO: 200ms (latency-first) with a cost target of $0.003/100 tokens for bulk operations.

3) Embeddings & reranker
   - Indexing: run batch embeddings using redwood-embed-1 then incremental updates for new documents.
   - Reranker: use a smaller (but accurate) reranker model post-retrieval to improve precision; we can provide a tuning guide.

4) Structured output & tool-calling
   - If you need structured JSON outputs or third-party tool calls (DB lookups), we recommend using our tool-calling shim + schema validation to avoid drift.

Next steps / asks:
- Can you share a small sample (100-200 docs) for evaluation? Prefer pseudonymized data.
- Confirm whether OpsCo requires Private (VPC) deployment or Hosted with KMS.
- Schedule a 45-minute technical follow-up with Rachel (solutions engineer) to walk through SDK auth and routing sample.

Attachments: architecture-diagram.png (high-level), routing-policy-example.yaml (sample policy).

I'll follow up with an annotated policy example and quickstart link.

Thanks,
Dev

--

Sample routing policy (we'll put this into the drive doc):

# routing-policy-example.yaml
version: 1
policies:
  - name: default-user-facing
    type: latency_first
    p95_target_ms: 200
    primary: redwood-rt-lowlat@us-east
    fallbacks:
      - redwood-llama-13b-quant@us-east
      - redwood-llama-7b-quant@us-east
    schedule:
      - window: "09:00-18:00"
        days: "Mon-Fri"
        preference: latency
      - window: "18:00-09:00"
        days: "Mon-Fri,Sat,Sun"
        preference: cost
  - name: eu-requests
    type: region_route
    region: eu-west
    primary: redwood-rt-lowlat@eu-west

Alice — quick follow-up with explicit examples so your engineers can review ahead of the call. 

Example SDK call (node) with routing override:

const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
const response = await client.generate({
  model: 'redwood-rt-lowlat',
  input: userQuery,
  routing: { policy: 'default-user-facing', overrides: { preference: 'latency' } },
  stream: true
});

Auth notes:
- API Key: fastest to start for PoC. Scoped keys available per-service.
- OAuth/service accounts: required if you'd like user-scoped access and SSO integration.
- Private deployment: we will enable VPC + KMS and exchange certs; Rachel can share the checklist.

Latency/cost policy details (engineer-friendly):
- Policy engine evaluates in order: (1) region constraint, (2) hard constraints (e.g., max_latency_ms), (3) budget/cost soft thresholds.
- Soft threshold example: if observed cost > target for a rolling 1h window, reduce primary model concurrency to shift some traffic to cheaper fallback; if latency breaches SLO, immediately prioritize latency-first fallbacks.
- We support scheduled policies and dynamic thresholds via our metrics API (you can write triggers based on real-time p95 or cost-per-token).

Embeddings + reranker latency:
- Typical retrieval (vector DB) + rerank on redwood-rt-small: ~80-150ms depending on shard/config. Reranker adds ~50-120ms; combined still within your 300ms target in most configs. We'll validate with your dataset.

Next steps:
1) Please confirm whether you want Hosted (fast onboarding) or Private (VPC/KMS) so Rachel can prepare the deployment checklist.
2) Share the 100-200 doc sample here.
3) Confirm Wed 10am PT (or propose).

Attachments: quickstart-sample.zip, routing-policy-example.yaml

Thanks — looking forward to the demo.

Dev
